reason: E1 provides direct evidence that substrate preheating reduces residual stresses, supporting one key premise. However, the cited evidence does not address compositional segregation, defect formation, or mechanical property improvements in AlCrFeNiSi or any HEA; E2 discusses post-process heat treatment for segregation in a different alloy, not in-situ preheating during AM. Thus, most premises lack specific prior support.
premises: Substrate preheating reduces longitudinal residual stresses in the build direction
Reduced thermal gradients from preheating mitigate compositional segregation
Reduced thermal gradients from preheating lower defect formation (cracks, porosity)
More uniform microstructure from preheating improves mechanical integrity (strength and ductility)
